about.title: Salinas Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When someone dies because of another person's carelessness, the paperwork arrives before the grief has room to settle. Public records for 2025 list 410 injury collisions across Salinas, 560 people hurt, and one traffic fatality — a single number that stands for a whole household. The highest collision counts in the city fall along N Main Street, E Market Street, E Laurel Drive and E Boronda Road, and reported crashes tend to peak on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. Not every wrongful death begins on a road, though. A fall at a job site, a missed diagnosis, a product that failed — each can support a civil claim under California law, one that runs on its own track apart from any criminal case. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Monterey County families, at no charge, with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death matters on contingency. You decide what happens next, and there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What Salinas Families Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Standing is limited under California law
items.desc: A surviving spouse or domestic partner and children have the first right to bring a wrongful death claim; certain dependents and heirs may qualify only when those relatives are absent. An attorney can sort out who in your family is eligible.

items.title: The two-year clock starts on the date of death
items.desc: California generally gives families two years from the date of death to file, and the window is considerably shorter when a city, county or state agency may be responsible. Early legal guidance protects that deadline.

items.title: Losses go beyond funeral bills
items.desc: Recoverable damages can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. None of it is guaranteed, but all of it can be claimed.

items.question: The crash that killed my relative happened on E Boronda Road and a Salinas city vehicle was involved. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It can change the timeline significantly. When a government entity such as the City of Salinas or Monterey County may share fault, California requires a formal claim to be filed with that agency well before the usual two-year deadline — often within months. Because the shorter window is easy to miss during a period of mourning, it helps to speak with an attorney soon.

items.question: There is already a criminal case against the driver. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, they are separate matters. The criminal case is brought by the district attorney and focuses on punishment, not on compensating your family. A wrongful death claim is a civil action you control, and it can proceed regardless of whether the criminal case ends in a conviction.
